finding.claim: Stored iconUrl is user-supplied with no validation and is fetched server-side by the nightly job (indirect/stored SSRF). Host and scheme are fully attacker-controlled. The default HttpClient does not follow redirects unless configured, but the target can still be an internal host or the cloud metadata endpoint, and the response is read as bytes. Severity MEDIUM, since the endpoint is authenticated and the fetch happens later in a job. The webhookUrl sink at line 21 is not flagged: its anchored full-string regex is equivalent to exact matching.

trace.note: update(String webhook, String icon): icon comes from the PUT /profile request
this.iconUrl = icon stored with no validation (only webhook is checked at line 12)
nightly sync(HttpClient c) reads the stored iconUrl
URI.create(iconUrl) is passed to c.send as a GET with no allowlist, so the fetch reaches the attacker-chosen host

finding.guards_checked: No validation on icon in update() or sync(). The regex at line 12 covers only webhook. There is no scheme or host allowlist, no IP or RFC-1918 block, and no re-validation at fetch time. Redirect handling depends on the caller-supplied HttpClient, whose configuration is not shown. Direct internal or metadata targets are reachable regardless.

verdict.reason: src/Profile.java:16 stores the `icon` argument from update() unvalidated (the regex at line 12 covers only webhook), and sync() at src/Profile.java:23 passes it to URI.create and c.send with no scheme or host check.
